title: Bivariate Within- and Between-Cluster Correlations
text: wbCorr computes within- -cluster correlations clustered data, daily diary data repeated measures nested persons, data dyads teams. data, two variables can related two ways: Within clusters: person scores higher usual one variable, also score higher usual ? clusters: persons higher average one variable also higher average ? two correlations can differ size even sign. correlation rows mixes . wbCorr reports separately, p-values, confidence intervals, intraclass correlations (ICCs). use wbCorr, please cite : Küng, P. (2026). wbCorr: Bivariate Within- -Cluster Correlations. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20357592

title: Bivariate Within- and Between-Cluster Correlations
text: package includes simulated daily diary data. 100 participants reported three variables (var1, var2, var3) 50 days. data simulated within-person correlations positive -person correlations negative. summary() shows levels one matrix. Within-person correlations diagonal, -person correlations , ICCs diagonal. var1 var2, two levels point opposite directions. days participants report higher var1 usual, also report slightly higher var2 (r = 0.12). participants higher average var1 lower average var2 (r = -0.60). get_table() returns full results test statistics, degrees freedom, confidence intervals, p-values: plot() shows data behind correlation. lower panels show scatterplots regression line outliers red. upper panels show correlation significance stars.
code: library(wbCorr)  data("simdat_intensive_longitudinal") diary <- simdat_intensive_longitudinal[c("participantID", "var1", "var2", "var3")]  correlations <- wbCorr(diary, cluster = "participantID") summary(correlations, "wb") #> $merged_wb #>          var1    var2    var3 #> var1   [0.51] 0.12*** 0.79*** #> var2 -0.60***  [0.49] 0.29*** #> var3   -0.24*   -0.04  [0.49] #>  #> $note #> [1] "***p < 0.001, **p < 0.01, *p < 0.05" get_table(correlations) #> $within #>   Parameter1 Parameter2 pearson's r t-statistic   df       95% CI         p #> 1       var1       var2        0.12        8.53 4899 [0.09, 0.15] < .001*** #> 2       var1       var3        0.79       89.04 4899 [0.78, 0.80] < .001*** #> 3       var2       var3        0.29       21.50 4899 [0.27, 0.32] < .001*** #>  #> $between #>   Parameter1 Parameter2 pearson's r t-statistic df         95% CI         p #> 1       var1       var2       -0.60       -7.46 98 [-0.71, -0.46] < .001*** #> 2       var1       var3       -0.24       -2.43 98 [-0.42, -0.04]    0.017* #> 3       var2       var3       -0.04       -0.44 98  [-0.24, 0.15]     0.659 plot(correlations, "within") plot(correlations, "between")

title: Bivariate Within- and Between-Cluster Correlations
text: example, cluster bootstrap resamples whole persons, confidence intervals account dependence within persons:
code: set.seed(2026) bootstrapped <- wbCorr(diary, cluster = "participantID", inference = "cluster_bootstrap") get_table(bootstrapped, "between") #> $between #>   Parameter1 Parameter2 pearson's r      BC 95% CI bootstrap p #> 1       var1       var2       -0.60 [-0.70, -0.47]   < .001*** #> 2       var1       var3       -0.24 [-0.42, -0.04]      0.018* #> 3       var2       var3       -0.04  [-0.22, 0.12]       0.610

title: Bivariate Within- and Between-Cluster Correlations
text: variable split cluster means (part) deviations means (within part). Cluster means use available observations variable, psych::statsBy(). correlation uses rows variables observed. Within-cluster correlations correlate deviations. Tests use N - k - 1 degrees freedom, N number complete pairs k number clusters come . tests treat deviations independent, approximation. cluster bootstrap make assumption. -cluster correlations correlate cluster means. Tests use k - 2 degrees freedom. Pearson p-values use t distribution. Spearman p-values analytic confidence intervals use Fisher z-transformation. cluster bootstrap reports bias-corrected (BC) confidence intervals. ICC ICC(1,1) one-way random-effects model, estimated ANOVA mean squares. Use numeric binary variables. wbCorr converts ordered factors level numbers; analyze method = "auto" "spearman". Dummy-code nominal variables use. See ?wbCorr details.

Supported methods 'pearson', 'spearman', 'auto' (default: 'pearson'). 'pearson': p-values use t-statistics confidence intervals use Fisher z-transformation. 'spearman': p-values confidence intervals use Fisher z-transformation. 'auto': uses Spearman pairs ordered factor Pearson otherwise (reported point-biserial phi coefficient binary variables). nboot Specifies amount bootstrap samples (default: 1000). inference string specifying p-values confidence intervals computed. 'analytic' (default) uses formulas described method. 'cluster_bootstrap' resamples whole clusters computes bias-corrected (BC) bootstrap confidence intervals p-values. Unlike analytic tests, accounts dependence within clusters assume normal data. Use set.seed() reproducible results. 'none' returns correlation coefficients . between_weighting string. 'equal_clusters' (default), every cluster mean weighted -cluster correlations, even clusters contributed fewer measurement points. 'cluster_size', cluster means weighted number observations cluster variables. methods equivalent datasets without missing data equal number measurements per cluster.

title: wbCorr 0.3.2
text: Reimplemented one-way random-effects, single-measure ICC(1,1) ANOVA method--moments formula unequal cluster sizes. Negative sample ICCs retained, non-estimable cases now return explicit diagnostics. Corrected Pearson analytic degrees freedom Fisher-z confidence intervals. Intervals bounded -1 1, inference supported available analysis units reported unavailable. Clarified Spearman option descriptive correlation mean-centered scores within clusters cluster means clusters. Unsupported analytic, row-jackknife, cluster-size-weighted Spearman inference removed; whole-cluster bootstrap intervals remain available.

title: wbCorr 0.3.2
text: Strengthened validation data, cluster identifiers, method, confidence levels, bootstrap settings, weighting, centering choices. Logical variables declared two-level factors supported explicit 0/1 orientation. categorical inputs rejected guidance, non-finite numeric values treated missing. Detailed tables now retain every requested variable pair, including pairs whose coefficient inference estimated. Pair-specific observation counts, cluster counts, coefficient status, inference status, reasons, bootstrap yield diagnostics reported. Correlation-matrix diagonals 1 variables positive variance relevant level; otherwise NA. Added positive-semidefinite diagnostics unrounded within- -cluster matrices. Pairwise matrices positive semidefinite now trigger targeted warning, missing_data = "listwise" provides optional common-row analysis. get_matrix(..., numeric = TRUE) now returns unrounded numeric within, , merged matrices, including unrounded ICC diagonals. print() now provides concise, executable guidance inspecting summaries extracting full tables, numeric matrices, ICCs. Plot panels now use exact pair-specific rows, centering rule, method, -cluster weights used fitted object. Annotations come stored coefficient p-value, significance legends omitted p-values requested unavailable. to_excel() now accepts data frame matrix directly, supports mixed lists tabular objects, errors clearly nothing write, invisibly returns supplied output path.

title: wbCorr 0.3.2
text: Added reference tests psych::statsBy() within- -cluster correlations ICC(1,1), expanded automated regression-test coverage. Added pkgdown website workflow vignette introducing distinction within- -cluster correlations. Removed obsolete self-generated test fixtures, generated plot file, tracked R session history. Added safeguards including regenerated session graphics artifacts repository source package. Corrected bundled-data documentation report 5,000 observations 100 participants measured 50 days.
